title: Minimum Operations to Make a Rotated Palindrome II
hints: As in Part 1, for a rotation by r positions the answer candidate is r plus the sum of the cyclic letter distances over all mirrored pairs. The challenge is computing this sum for every rotation efficiently.

The cyclic distance between two lowercase letters can be represented using 13 binary features. For each k from 0 to 12, mark a letter if it belongs to the 13 consecutive cyclic letters starting at k. The cyclic distance between two letters equals the number of these features on which they differ.

For one such feature, create a binary array a over the positions of s. If cnt is the number of ones, then for a reflection represented by c, the number of mirrored pairs with different feature values is cnt - conv[c], where conv[c] = sum(a[i] * a[(c - i) mod n]).
Compute these circular self-convolutions for all 13 features using FFT or NTT. For a left rotation by r, use c = (2 * r - 1) mod n, sum the 13 contributions, and minimize this palindrome cost plus r.
